name: The Bail Project
summary: A US nonprofit, set up in 2016 in Venice, California, and bailing people out since 2018, that pays bail through a national revolving fund for people who can't afford it, supports them until their cases close (court reminders, rides, referrals), runs community-release pilots where cash bail has ended, and campaigns against laws that expand pretrial detention or restrict charitable bail. In the year to June 2025 it spent $13.9 million (Form 990; $16.3 million in the audited statements with a $2.3 million write-off of bail and pledges) at 14 bail sites in 10 states, down from 31 sites two years earlier as revenue fell.

spending.source: The Bail Project, Form 990 for July 2024 to June 2025 (IRS e-file 202620619349300142, EIN 81-4985512), Part IX line 25 column (B): programme service expenses $10,270,968 of total expenses $13,872,645; the return reports one programme. The audited statements' total of $16,254,891 adds a $2,284,937 loss on uncollectible pledges, loans and bail receivables (a catch-up of several years) and $97,309 of donated services (Schedule D Part XII).

lines.label: Bail assistance and client support (revolving bail fund, Bail Disruptors, rides and reminders, community-release pilots, grants to partner bail funds)
lines.source: Form 990 for July 2024 to June 2025, Part IX: 62% of programme service expenses of $10,270,968 (facts/the_bail_project.json bail_share_fy2025, our judgment from fiscal 2024's published split: Bail Assistance & Client Support $6,499,138 of $10,460,596, Annual Report 2024 pp. 50-51); the fiscal-2025 accounts give no split.

lines.label: Policy advocacy, public education, and research and evaluation
lines.source: Form 990 for July 2024 to June 2025, Part IX: the other 38% of programme service expenses of $10,270,968 (facts/the_bail_project.json bail_share_fy2025); in fiscal 2024 the three accounts lines were Policy Advocacy $1,204,975, Public Education $1,433,268 and Research & Evaluation $1,323,215 (Annual Report 2024 pp. 50-51). One model covers the three, as one set of campaigns.
